title: Understanding Non-Split 2-Group Symmetry: (3+1)D SymTFT, Anomaly and Bordism
authors: Zhenbang Gu, Ran Luo, Yi-Nan Wang, Yi Zhang
abstract: We present a systematic study of finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with a non-trivial Postnikov class, focusing on the simplest example with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry, intertwined together by the non-trivial Postnikov class in $H^3(B\mathbb{Z}_2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$, denoted by $\mathcal{G}$. We classify the anomalies of this 2-group symmetry for physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime, by computing the oriented bordism groups $Ω_{d+1}^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G})$ and the spin bordism groups $Ω_{d+1}^{\rm Spin}(B\mathcal{G})$ for $d\leq 5$. For the case of $d=3$, we investigate the Symmetry TFT/TO of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$ using the language of fusion 2-categories, as well as (3+1)D TQFT actions, for the cases without or with the 2-group anomaly classified by $\operatorname{Hom}\left(\widetildeΩ_4^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G}),U(1)\right) \cong H^4(B\mathcal{G};U(1))\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$. We classify the minimal topological and physical boundary conditions of the Symmetry TFTs, and carry out the categorical Landau paradigm for such non-split finite 2-group.
summary: This work provides a deep theoretical analysis of physical systems governed by non-split 2-group symmetries. By employing advanced tools from algebraic topology and category theory, the authors classify quantum anomalies and map out the landscape of possible topological and physical boundary phases for (3+1)D TQFTs.
main_problem: The paper systematically studies finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with non-trivial Postnikov classes in the context of (3+1)D Topological Quantum Field Theories (TQFTs). It aims to classify associated anomalies and boundary conditions.
main_result: The authors classified anomalies by computing oriented and spin bordism groups for low dimensions ($d \le 5$) and identified multiple minimal Lagrangian algebras corresponding to different topological and physical boundary phases.
method: The methodology combines advanced algebraic topology (bordism theory, cohomology) with categorical methods (fusion 2-categories) applied to TQFT formalism. They analyze the structure of weak 2-group symmetries.
model_or_system: The focus is on physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime exhibiting a non-split 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$. The analysis covers both gapped and gapless phases, relating to Symmetry Protected Topological (SPT) phases.
key_observables: Anomalies classified by cohomology groups like $H^4(B\mathcal{G}; U(1)) \cong \mathbb{Z}_2$, and the identification of various boundary conditions (e.g., symmetric, partial SSB, G-SPT).
important_parameters: The dimension of spacetime ($d$), the structure of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$, and the non-trivial Postnikov class.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the weak 2-group formulation and may require assuming a twisted spin structure on the underlying manifold for certain calculations.
figures_summary: Tables summarize calculated bordism groups (Table 1) and different physical boundary conditions/phases (Table 2). Figures illustrate defect interactions and the physical meaning of the Postnikov class.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the non-split 2-group symmetry, calculating its anomalies using bordism theory for $d \le 5$, then applying this to construct and classify the resulting Symmetry TQFTs ($	ext{SymTFT}$) and their boundary conditions via categorical methods.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting higher-dimensional topological field theories, generalized symmetries (2-groups), and anomaly classification is highly relevant for understanding exotic phases of matter beyond standard Landau theory in condensed matter physics.
